m0.speaker: Marla — night clerk
m0.text:
You're not from the bank and you're not from the state, so I'm going to guess press. Third lot this month.

Checkout's eleven. Ice machine's been broke since the mill closed, which tells you about how long that's been.

choices.text: We're looking into the deaths. Six men in five weeks.
Just a room. And whatever's behind the counter.
What happened to this town, Marla?

m1.speaker: Marla — night clerk
m1.text:
Deaths. That's a polite word for it.

They were mill men. Every one of them worked the green chain. They got told the plant was losing money and they believed it, because what else do you do. Then the severance ran out.

choices.text: Six men, same method, same week of the month. That's not despair. That's a pattern.

m2.speaker: Marla — night clerk
m2.text:
I think a man can be killed slow and the paperwork still says he did it himself.

But no. Not just. Ray Hollis was the happiest of them. Bought a boat in March. In April he wouldn't cross the lot after dark, said the streetlights were watching him wrong.

m2b.speaker: Marla — night clerk
m2b.text:
You've got a cop's mouth on you.

Fine. Pattern. They all went quiet the same way first. Stopped answering. Ray Hollis stopped crossing the lot after dark — said the streetlights were watching him wrong.

m3.speaker: Marla — night clerk
m3.text:
Said they'd hum when he was sad and go dark when he wasn't. Said the whole town got heavier around three in the morning, like something leaned on it.

I laughed at him. He's in the ground now and I still hear the hum some nights.

choices.text: You should leave. Tonight, if you can.

m4.speaker: Marla — night clerk
m4.text:
Crossroads Holdings. Out of Delaware, address is a mailbox. They bought it profitable and ran it into the dirt inside eleven months. Took the machines, left the asbestos.

Nobody's ever seen a single employee.

effects.log: Marla named the buyer: Crossroads Holdings.

m5.speaker: Marla — night clerk
m5.text:
East end, past the cross street. Door's chained but the chain's been cut since February — kids, probably.

Don't go at three.

m_town.speaker: Marla — night clerk
m_town.text:
Same thing that happened to every town like it. Somebody in a building I'll never see decided we cost more than we made.

The rest is just weather.

choices.text: That's not weather. That's a decision somebody signed.
Six men are dead. I need the specifics, not the eulogy.

m_drink.speaker: Marla — night clerk
m_drink.text:
There's a fifth of rye under here older than you are. Costs eight dollars and it'll take the edge off tonight and put two more on tomorrow.

Your call, honey.

m_drank.speaker: Marla — night clerk
m_drank.text:
There he is.

The shake goes out of your hands and the town goes soft at the corners. It's the first quiet you've had in four states.

Something in the back of your skull files it away as a solution.

m_refused.speaker: Marla — night clerk
m_refused.text:
Suit yourself. Most men in here don't have that in them.

Your hands don't stop. The hum in the lot gets a half-step louder, and you notice you can hear it at all.

m_leave.speaker: Marla — night clerk
m_leave.text:
With what car, honey? With what money?

But — thank you. Nobody's said a thing like that to me in about two years.

p0.speaker: The shape on the green chain
p0.text:
It is a man made of sawdust and standing oil. Where its lungs were, the ASCII will not hold still.

"QUOTA," it says, and the word arrives inside your teeth rather than through the air. "QUOTA. QUOTA. THE VENT WAS ON THE FORM."

choices.text: [Salt and iron.] Put it down. It's already dead.
[Latin.] Try to let it finish the sentence first.

p_burn.text:
Rock salt takes it across the chest and it comes apart like a struck bag of flour.

It does not scream. It says "THANK" and the second word is eaten by a seam in the air that should not be there — a tear, thin as a paper cut, that closes with a wet sound.

Something ate your ghost. That's new.

effects.log: Something is consuming the dead in Oakhaven.

p_talk.speaker: The shape on the green chain
p_talk.text:
It stops. The oil on it goes still.

"FOURTEEN," it says. "VENT FOURTEEN. I FILED IT IN MARCH. I FILED IT IN MARCH. THEY SAID IT WAS CAPITAL EXPENDITURE."

It looks at its own hands like it's checking whether they're still on the form.

choices.text: They killed you with a spreadsheet. I know. Go.

p_rest.text:
It goes out like a pilot light — no violence in it at all.

And then the empty air where it stood puckers. A seam opens, thin as a paper cut, and drinks the last of it before closing with a wet sound.

Something is eating the dead here. Salting the bones was never going to be enough.

effects.log: Something is consuming the dead in Oakhaven.

d0.speaker: A regular
d0.text:
He doesn't look up. There are four empties in front of him and it isn't seven o'clock.

"If you're here about the mill, I got nothing. If you're here about Ray, I got less."

d1.speaker: A regular
d1.text:
Now he looks up.

"Everybody hears it and nobody says it, and you walk in off the highway and say it first thing."

He pushes a beer mat across the bar. Someone has written on it in ballpoint, over and over, in a hand that got worse as it went:

  while town.mood < 0.2: yield

"Found forty of these behind the dart board. Ray's writing. Ray couldn't type."

effects.log: Ray Hollis was transcribing something that looks like a scheduler loop.

k0.speaker: Kevin Tran
k0.text:
He is nineteen and looks forty. The light coming out of his eyes is the wrong colour for a room this dark.

"You're going to ask me to read it. Everyone asks me to read it. Last time I read it for four hours and afterwards I couldn't remember my mother's face for a week."

choices.text: Then don't read it. Sit down. We'll find another way.
I need the translation, Kevin. Now.
[Show him the fragments.] These aren't scripture. Look at the syntax.

k_detox.speaker: Kevin Tran
k_detox.text:
He stares at you like you've spoken a language he'd stopped expecting.

"Nobody's offered me that. Not once. Not the angels, not you two, not God."

It takes three days and he screams through most of them. On the fourth morning he asks for eggs, and his eyes are just eyes.

choices.text: Rest. We'll handle the rest of it.

effects.log: Kevin is lucid. That was not free.

k_burn.speaker: Kevin Tran
k_burn.text:
He reads for four hours. Something behind his face gives way around hour three and he keeps going anyway, because you asked.

When he stops, he can tell you exactly what the tablet says. He cannot tell you what year it is.

effects.log: You have the translation. Kevin does not have much left.

k_syntax.speaker: Kevin Tran
k_syntax.text:
He turns the beer mat over. Then the terminal printout. Then the third one.

His hands stop shaking, which is somehow worse.

"That's not Enochian. That's not any angelic tongue, I've read all of them." A long pause. "That's a while loop. Sam — that's a *while loop*."

effects.log: Kevin recognised the scripture as source code.
